page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY processor cores, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.se1ne.2xlarge exhibits modest compute and memory performance. The Intel Xeon 8269CY processor registers single-core and multi-core CPU performance in the bottom 25% tier under stress-ng testing, with Geekbench scores reflecting similar weak-to-poor performance profiles. While memory write bandwidth for large blocks is average at 34.3 GB/sec, read-only memory bandwidth remains in the bottom 25%. LLM inference tasks using a small 135M parameter model achieve average speeds of 464.73 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 99.23 tokens/sec for text generation, but performance drops significantly to the bottom 10% when executing a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.2xlarge offers a high memory capacity relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not demand high CPU throughput. However, its low compute benchmarks and limited 2 Gbps network bandwidth represent significant tradeoffs for processing-intensive tasks. This instance is best suited for workloads such as caching layers, lightweight database operations, and memory-intensive applications with moderate processing requirements.
